question: Music is an important driver of economic and cultural growth. The exponential growth of streaming platforms has transformed the music industry. Sector studies1 show that approximately 90 % of artists are present on streaming platforms, and that 80 % of them receive no or very little income from streaming.

A 2025 Commission study2 on contractual practices in certain creative sectors, including the music sector, focuses on the issue of the transfer of rights from authors/performers/producers to the contractual counterparts that exploit these rights.

This highlights the need to ensure fairer models of revenue distribution, full implementation of the right to adequate and proportionate remuneration – established by Directive (EU) 2019/7903– and greater transparency from streaming platforms. In this regard, Parliament adopted a resolution on cultural diversity and the conditions for authors in the European music streaming market on 17 January 20244.
In the light of the above, the Commission is asked: 1.
whether it intends to investigate the music streaming market to assess the effectiveness of the legislation and respect for artists’ right to fair remuneration?
whether it considers it necessary to propose transparency obligations and penalties for failure to communicate data on the use of phonograms?
whether it deems it appropriate to establish a ‘European industrial strategy for music’, as suggested by the Parliament resolution?

Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Usare la musica online – Artisti e musicisti nell’economia dello streaming, February 2024. European Commission, Study on contractual practices affecting the transfer of copyright and related rights and the ability of creators and producers to exploit their rights – Final Report, January 2025. OJ L 130, 17.5.2019, pp. 92–125, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/790/oj. OJ C, C/2024/5711, 17.10.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/C/2024/5711/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.10.2025) In accordance with Article 30 of Directive (EU) 2019/790 on copyright and related rights in the Digital Single Market, the Commission will carry out a review of the Directive not before 7 June 2026. The effectiveness of the Directive’s measures on the remuneration of authors and performers will be considered as part of this review.

In this context, the Commission will assess the implementation of the transparency obligations introduced under Article 19 of the Directive, taking into account the margin of manoeuvre of Member States to address specificities of the different content sectors.

Under this provision, music performers should receive relevant and comprehensive information on the exploitation of their performances fixed in phonograms from the parties to whom they have transferred their rights, or from sub-licensees. Based on the outcome of the review, the Commission will consider the way forward.

Regarding the establishment of a European industrial strategy for music, the Commission acknowledges the call made by the European Parliament and will continue to engage with stakeholders, including authors, artists, producers, and streaming services, to address the challenges facing the music industry and promote a fair and sustainable music ecosystem.
